question.text: Mr. Siddharth Rao, CIO of Kaveri Cat III AIF, is finalising the PPM's benchmark clause. The fund's pre-tax NAV reporting includes all dividends received on portfolio holdings. Per Section 10.5.6 of Chapter 10, which benchmark variant should he select to ensure a LIKE-FOR-LIKE comparison with the fund's NAV return?

answer.text: The price index variant (e.g., NIFTY 50), because dividends are irrelevant to benchmark construction.

The Total Return Index (TRI) variant (e.g., NIFTY 50 TRI), because TRI reinvests indexed dividends on the ex-date and thus captures both capital gains and dividend income — matching the AIF's NAV which also includes dividend accrual.
A dollar-denominated variant (e.g., NIFTY 50 USD), because the fund must report in USD for LP comparability.
An equal-weighted variant, because dividend yields are more uniform across equal-weighted constituents.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.5.6, a price index ONLY captures capital gains from price movement; dividends are excluded. Total Return Index (TRI) indexes dividend payouts on the ex-date and reinvests them into the index, giving a true return that is comparable to a fund NAV which also includes dividend accrual. 'An investor in index stocks should benchmark his investments against the Total Returns index instead of the price index.' The Trap: Option A produces a structurally biased comparison — price index will systematically understate benchmark return by ~1.5% p.a. on Indian large-caps, inflating apparent alpha. Option C addresses currency, not dividends. Option D conflates weighting with return computation. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) tests TRI vs price index for listed portfolios. XV (Research Analyst) tests return decomposition into capital and dividend components. Manager's Pro-Tip: In your PPM, state 'Benchmark: NIFTY 50 TRI (INR)' in full — NOT just 'NIFTY 50'. A diligent institutional LP will rewrite your numbers against TRI if you quoted price index, and your alpha narrative will collapse during fundraising DD.
